parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, no same-sex criminalisation, and no documented border, registration, facility or custody rule aimed at trans travellers — so nothing like the state apparatus that anchors 0.35–0.55. But the record also shows no working protection of any kind: no anti-discrimination statute, no gender-recognition route, no hate-crime recourse, an Article 5 domestic-violence clause that reaches only domestic violence, and a state context of impunity. Societal evidence is dated and contested (2011–12 stigma/taboos; a 2018 NGO reference to 'some cases' of SO/GI violence without figures). That combination — undocumented state exposure, documented absence of remedy, thin dated hostility — sits in Elevated Risk, above the friction-without-protection anchors only because no traveller-facing mechanism is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, visa or screening rule documented; no recorded marker-flagging or secondary inspection of gender-nonconforming visitors. No domestic gender-recognition route exists, but a visitor's marker is home-issued.
entry_documents.interaction: Border practice toward trans travellers is entirely unsourced; in a thin dossier this silence is not established safety.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented trans-specific arrest, detention or custody-placement rule or incident. General record shows security-force torture and impunity, not aimed at trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: General impunity would degrade any remedy after an incident, but no trans-specific custody exposure is evidenced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward, shelter or changing-room rule documented; no police registration or hotel-reporting duty documented. Housing-allowance restriction affects resident couples only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility and accommodation practice toward trans guests is unsourced; no universal-exposure measure evidenced.

care_services.exposure: 2012 reporting records no official discrimination in health care; no anti-discrimination statute covers gender identity, so refusal would carry no statutory claim.
care_services.protection: Article 5 of the 2014 domestic-violence law guarantees equal protection to all victims regardless of sexual orientation — domestic-violence context only.
care_services.interaction: Ward-placement and clinical practice for trans patients are unsourced; the protective clause does not generalise.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No law frames trans identity as a threat; no police targeting of gender-nonconforming people documented. 2018 NGO states legal protections for LGBTI people are absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented beyond the narrow Article 5 clause; the 2008 declaration has no domestic force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Absence of a hostile statute is a genuine positive; absence of any protective statute leaves the traveller without recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth- or minor-specific findings on health access, schooling or travel; no trans or LGBTQ minor evidence.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adults travelling with a trans minor face entirely unevidenced conditions; adoption and schooling positions unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2012 report found no reported SO/GI-based violence; 2018 NGO cites 'some cases' without figures, dates or location. No trans-specific data at all.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime or anti-discrimination recourse available to a victim.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Unquantified and conflicting; under weak rule of law an assault would likely go unpunished.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute, no gender-recognition procedure, no partnership recognition; 2012 reporting confirms anti-discrimination law does not apply to LGBT people.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Article 5 of the 2014 domestic-violence statute only; no enforcement body or complaint route evidenced.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller refused service or assaulted has no statutory claim, and impunity further weakens practical remedy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia has police instructed to stop trans visitors, seize documents, detain for hours and fine them. This dossier documents no police stop, seizure, detention or fine practice at all; only the absence of any remedy. Materially safer on the operative exposure axis, though the missing remedy is comparable.

Drellia imposes mandatory police registration, nightly hotel data transmission and repeated interviews — universal exposure reaching every trans visitor. None of that machinery is documented here; there is no registration duty, no reporting duty and no database linkage, so this jurisdiction sits above that anchor.

Kestrel Isles documents secondary screening, luggage searches, refused admission and humiliating interviews for document divergence. Here border practice toward trans travellers is unsourced, not documented as adverse. The absence of any protection is shared, so the gap is narrower than the anchor difference suggests.

Meridia has trained border officers, a tribunal hearing detention appeals, written reasons and compensation. This dossier has no equality statute, no complaint body and no compensation route, so it sits clearly below that tier despite sharing the absence of any criminalisation of trans identity.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime contains no hostile rule the traveller must pass through: no criminalisation of same-sex conduct or gender expression, no documented border screening, no registration or hotel-reporting duty, no facility or custody-placement rule, and 2012 reporting found no official discrimination in health care, employment or education. What is missing is everything protective: no anti-discrimination statute, no gender-recognition route, no hate-crime recourse, and a state context of documented impunity. Societal evidence is dated and contradictory — 2011–12 stigma and taboos against 2012 findings of relative tolerance, and a bare 2018 reference to 'some cases' of violence without figures. Unknowns (border practice, ward and custody placement) are unevidenced rather than adverse, so they are weighted lightly; the documented absence of remedy is weighted fully.
